legal.privacy.p02: This Privacy Policy explains what information Hollywoodland (the "Game"), operated by Playology Entertainment ("Playology," "we," "us," or "our"), collects and how it is used. We designed the Game to collect as little information as possible.
legal.privacy.p04: The Game requires no account, name, email address, or password to play. Your career — the name you give your character, the origin and character you choose, and your progress — is stored only in your browser's local storage (IndexedDB) and is never sent to our servers automatically.
legal.privacy.p05: If you choose to export a save file, that file is saved to your own device; we only receive it if you voluntarily send it to us, for example to report a bug.
legal.privacy.p06: The Settings menu includes an optional toggle to share anonymous, aggregate performance analytics; it does not send your character's name, dialogue, or save data, and you can turn it off at any time.
legal.privacy.p09: Require account registration with personal information.

legal.privacy.p15: How We Store and Protect Information
legal.privacy.p16: Your career and save data live in your browser's own storage, under your control; a save file you export is a plain file on your device. We take reasonable measures to protect any information we do receive, but no method of electronic storage or transmission is completely secure.
legal.privacy.p18: We do not sell your information. We do not share it with third parties, except with service providers who help us operate the Game (such as hosting or analytics infrastructure) or if required to do so by law.
legal.privacy.p20: The Game is intended for a general audience and does not knowingly collect personal information from children. Playing the Game does not require a name, email address, or any other personal information.
legal.privacy.p22: Because your progress is stored only in your browser, clearing your browser's site data or switching to a different browser or device will make it inaccessible unless you exported a save file first. You can turn off anonymous analytics sharing at any time in Settings.

content.dialogue.casting-office-intro.ro: "Appointment, photograph, or miracle?" she asks, barely glancing up.
You mentioned a screen test. (-10 Energy)
content.dialogue.casting-office-intro.sc: "Stage 4, dress in the dress. They’re waiting on you." She slides a dog-eared script across the counter.
content.dialogue.casting-office-intro.ph: "Not bad. Can you read for us Tuesday?"
Mention a contact on the lot.
Any word on the audition? (-10 Energy)
Ask if she can slot you in earlier.
Mention you have already been through one callback.
Show her the studio headshot from your last callback.
content.dialogue.casting-office-intro.mi: "Everyone wants a miracle. Come back with a photograph."
Remind her you already showed one.
content.dialogue.casting-office-intro.fa: "Oh — well, that changes things. Tuesday, front of the line."
"You landed it? Good. Keep that up and we’ll talk about the next one."
"Don’t make me regret this. Monday, then — first thing."
content.dialogue.sunset-diner-intro.root: "Coffee, doll? You look like you could use it," she says, already reaching for the pot.
content.dialogue.sunset-diner-intro.sett: "So, what brings a face like yours to this end of the Boulevard?"
What is the real story on this town? (-10 Energy)
Read the room, then ask about the gossip column.
content.dialogue.sunset-diner-intro.goss: "Ask around enough and you will hear it all — who is bankable, who is trouble, and who is both."
content.dialogue.boarding-house-intro.ro: "Rent's due Friday, same as always," she says, not looking up from her ledger.
Here — this week, paid in full.
Could I get a few more days?
content.dialogue.boarding-house-intro.se: "Just so we are clear where we stand," she says, setting down her pen.
I am good for it — steady work is coming. (-10 Energy)
Show her the callback slip from your last audition. (-10 Energy)
content.dialogue.backlot-gate-intro.root: "Well, look who else got called back," she says, looking you up and down.
Look her up and down right back.
Same casting call, huh? Small town.
content.dialogue.backlot-gate-intro.sizi: "Let's see who's still standing after the next round of cuts," she says, but it sounds almost like a dare.
May the best actress win. (-10 Energy)
Careful — I don't lose easily. (-10 Energy)
content.dialogue.extras-corral-intro.roo: "Name?" he snaps, pen already hovering over the sign-in sheet. "Corral fills up fast — I do not have all morning."
Give your name and step back to wait.
Apologize — traffic on the Boulevard held you up.
content.dialogue.extras-corral-intro.che: "You're on the list," he says, already scanning past you toward the corral. "Stay behind the rope until someone waves you onto the set."
Ask what today's call actually needs from the extras. (-10 Energy)
Mention the callback slip from the casting office. (-10 Energy)
Say nothing and wait for the wave-in.
content.dialogue.soundstage-intro.root.t: "You're covering my mark today?" she asks, flipping through her sides. "Let's at least get through it once before they roll film."
content.dialogue.soundstage-intro.root.c: Offer to run the scene twice before the crew is ready.
Play it too big, daring her to match you.
content.dialogue.soundstage-intro.settle: "Places in five," the assistant director calls from off camera. "You've got until then to find it," she says, script still in hand.
Play it exactly as blocked — no surprises. (-10 Energy)
Dig into what your characters actually want from each other. (-10 Energy)
Tell her you could get used to rehearsing with her. (-10 Energy)
content.dialogue.silver-thimble-intro.ro: "Mind the pins, and keep your hands off the silk," she says, a yellow tape measure trailing from her neck. "Half of Monarch's call sheet is hanging in this shop, and every seam on it is mine."
Admire the swashbuckler's coat on the rack.
Ask whether she has a minute to size up a newcomer.
content.dialogue.silver-thimble-intro.co: "The Corsair's Daughter," she says, smoothing a sleeve. "Forty yards of braid, and not one of those pirates can sit down in it. Ask me how I know."
Ask whether she could spare a minute for you, too.
Let her get back to the braid.
content.dialogue.silver-thimble-intro.fi: "Chin level, shoulders down, and do not breathe in," she says, chalk already moving. "A costume that fits is worth more to a career than a good headshot. Come back when you have a callback."
Thank her and promise to come back.
"Fresh face, no entourage, suitcase still on the shoulder," he says, notebook already raised. "Give me something I can print, and I'll owe you one."
Give him a harmless bit of color about your arrival.
Ask what he has heard about Monarch's casting.
Smile and say you have nothing to print.
content.dialogue.klieg-light-intro.tip-r: "Wholesome. My editor will hate it," he grins, scribbling. "But a name in print is a name people remember. Remember who put it there."
Tip your hat and head out.
content.dialogue.klieg-light-intro.gossi: "Monarch's casting is a revolving door, and Sunset Casting Exchange holds the key," he says, lowering his voice. "Be early and be reliable, and they forget you're new. Be a story, and I'll be the one who tells it."
content.dialogue.klieg-light-intro.cool-: "Everybody's got something," he says, tipping his hat back with the pencil. "You know where the desk is."
Walk back out onto the Boulevard.
A silver-templed man in a maroon tailcoat straightens from the velvet rope and sweeps a white glove toward the ceiling. "Welcome to the Celestial Palace," he says. "The feature does not start until the evening show, but the lobby is always open to those who can appreciate it."
Step back out to the Boulevard.

"Every star up there is gold leaf, set by hand," he says, with the pride of a man reciting a family history. "They say that if you stand under the sunburst long enough, the industry notices you. Mostly it gives you a stiff neck."
Rub your neck and head out.
"Monarch's new swashbuckler, The Corsair's Daughter, opens next month," he says, tapping an empty poster frame with the brass flashlight. "Until then it is newsreels and a cartoon."

"A Monarch voucher?" He straightens further, if that is possible, and lowers his voice. "Crew and extras sit free at the Tuesday matinee, and nobody asks where you got the seat. Ask for me at the rope."
